title.fa: «فروکاست تفکر»: روایت گومبروویچ از فلسفه پس از کانت
title.en: "The reduction of thought": Gombrowicz’s story of philosophy after Kant
title.nl: "The reduction of thought": Gombrowicz’s story of philosophy after Kant

summary.fa: گومبروویچ تمام فلسفهٔ دو قرن گذشته را با یک خط می‌خواند: فروکاست. با کانت، آگاهی برای نخستین بار از مرزهای خودش می‌پرسد، و از آن پس هر فیلسوف بزرگ دامنهٔ ادعای فلسفه را تنگ‌تر می‌کند — تا جایی که پرسش «جهان را چگونه توضیح دهیم؟» جایش را به «جهان را چگونه تغییر دهیم؟» می‌دهد.
summary.en: Gombrowicz reads two centuries of philosophy along a single line: reduction. With Kant, consciousness asks for the first time about its own limits, and after him every major philosopher narrows philosophy’s claim — until the question "how can the world be explained?" gives way to "how can the world be changed?"
summary.nl: Gombrowicz reads two centuries of philosophy along a single line: reduction. With Kant, consciousness asks for the first time about its own limits, and after him every major philosopher narrows philosophy’s claim — until the question "how can the world be explained?" gives way to "how can the world be changed?"

text.fa: نقطهٔ آغاز نزد او دکارت است و «ایدهٔ بزرگ» دکارت «حذف ابژه»: شبی مطلق را مجسم کنید که ابژه‌ای را در بر گرفته است؛ اگر ذهنی نباشد که آن را ادراک کند، آن ابژه هم وجود ندارد. از همین‌جا فلسفه آگاهی را امری بنیادین می‌بیند.
text.en: His starting point is Descartes, whose "great idea" was the elimination of the object: imagine an absolute night enclosing an object; if there is no mind to perceive it, the object does not exist either. From here philosophy begins to treat consciousness as fundamental.
text.nl: His starting point is Descartes, whose "great idea" was the elimination of the object: imagine an absolute night enclosing an object; if there is no mind to perceive it, the object does not exist either. From here philosophy begins to treat consciousness as fundamental.

text.fa: ولی گومبروویچ می‌گوید دکارت از پیامدهای مهیب فکر خودش ترسید و کوشید نشان دهد خدا — و در نتیجه جهان به‌عنوان مخلوق او — واقعیتی ابژکتیو است؛ تمام فلسفهٔ پسین او از همین ترس دچار انحراف شد. همین ترس را بعدها در سارتر هم می‌بیند.
text.en: But Gombrowicz says Descartes took fright at the terrible consequences of his own thought and tried to show that God — and hence the world as God’s creature — is an objective reality; his whole later philosophy was deflected by that fear. He sees the same fright later in Sartre.
text.nl: But Gombrowicz says Descartes took fright at the terrible consequences of his own thought and tried to show that God — and hence the world as God’s creature — is an objective reality; his whole later philosophy was deflected by that fear. He sees the same fright later in Sartre.

text.fa: کانت نزد او نقطهٔ عطف است: نقد خرد ناب در واقع دربارهٔ نقد خرد نیست، بلکه دربارهٔ این است که «چگونه می‌توانیم دربارهٔ آگاهی خودمان داوری کنیم» — آگاهی دربارهٔ آگاهی داوری می‌کند. پرسش بنیادین: آدمی تا کجا می‌تواند به آگاهی اعتماد کند؟
text.en: Kant is his turning point: the Critique of Pure Reason is not really about criticizing reason but about how we can judge our own consciousness — consciousness judging consciousness. The basic question: how far can a person trust consciousness?
text.nl: Kant is his turning point: the Critique of Pure Reason is not really about criticizing reason but about how we can judge our own consciousness — consciousness judging consciousness. The basic question: how far can a person trust consciousness?

text.fa: نتیجهٔ کانت آن است که خرد ما ضرورتاً به جهان پدیداری محدود است و هرگز نمی‌توانیم فارغ از شیوه‌های ادراکمان بدانیم نومن چیست. گومبروویچ این را با مثالی روزمره می‌گوید: همان ابژه با عینک زرد و از چشم یک مورچه (که دوبعدی می‌بیند) تغییر کرده است.
text.en: Kant’s upshot is that our reason is necessarily confined to the phenomenal world and we can never know what the noumenon is apart from our modes of perception. Gombrowicz puts it with an everyday example: the same object has changed when seen through yellow glasses and through the eyes of an ant that sees in two dimensions.
text.nl: Kant’s upshot is that our reason is necessarily confined to the phenomenal world and we can never know what the noumenon is apart from our modes of perception. Gombrowicz puts it with an everyday example: the same object has changed when seen through yellow glasses and through the eyes of an ant that sees in two dimensions.

text.fa: کلید روایت او: «با کانت فروکاست بزرگِ تفکر آغاز می‌شود، فرایندی که تا امروز ادامه یافته است.» و این فروکاست نشان ضعف نیست، نشان بلوغ است: تفکر شروع کرده است به شناختن مرزهای خویش.
text.en: The key to his narrative: "with Kant the great reduction of thought begins, a process that has continued to today." And this reduction is not a sign of weakness but of maturity: thought has begun to know its own limits.
text.nl: The key to his narrative: "with Kant the great reduction of thought begins, a process that has continued to today." And this reduction is not a sign of weakness but of maturity: thought has begun to know its own limits.

text.fa: زنجیرهٔ فروکاست‌هایی که او می‌شمارد: فویرباخ؛ مارکس (آگاهی تابعی از زندگی است و «هستی» تعیین‌کنندهٔ آگاهی)؛ پدیدارشناسی هوسرل، که در آن فلسفه دیگر در پی واقعیت چیزها یا حقیقت نیست بلکه صرفاً مرتب کردن امور واقع آگاهی است؛ و فروکاست روانکاوانهٔ فروید — که به نظر او از جنس بقیه نیست چون ماهیتی علمی دارد.
text.en: The chain of reductions he lists: Feuerbach; Marx (consciousness as a function of life, with "being" determining consciousness); Husserl’s phenomenology, in which philosophy no longer seeks the reality of things or truth but merely orders the facts of consciousness; and Freud’s psychoanalytic reduction — which in his view is of a different kind because it is scientific.
text.nl: The chain of reductions he lists: Feuerbach; Marx (consciousness as a function of life, with "being" determining consciousness); Husserl’s phenomenology, in which philosophy no longer seeks the reality of things or truth but merely orders the facts of consciousness; and Freud’s psychoanalytic reduction — which in his view is of a different kind because it is scientific.

text.fa: نتیجهٔ تاریخی که می‌گیرد: «امروزه فلسفه شامل جستجوی حقیقتی مطلق، مثل وجود خدا، نمی‌شود؛ بسیار محدودتر شده و به جهان پدیداری بسنده کرده است»، و پرسش «جهان را چگونه می‌شود توضیح داد؟» جایش را به پرسش مارکس داده است: «جهان را چگونه می‌شود تغییر داد؟»
text.en: His historical conclusion: "philosophy today no longer involves the search for an absolute truth such as the existence of God; it has become far narrower and settled for the phenomenal world," and "how can the world be explained?" has given way to Marx’s question, "how can the world be changed?"
text.nl: His historical conclusion: "philosophy today no longer involves the search for an absolute truth such as the existence of God; it has become far narrower and settled for the phenomenal world," and "how can the world be explained?" has given way to Marx’s question, "how can the world be changed?"

text.fa: خط دوم روایت او «شدن» است: پیش از هگل فلسفه مدعی توصیف دنیایی ثابت بود و حرکت مسئلهٔ اساسی نبود؛ فلسفهٔ هگل فلسفهٔ شدن است و ایدهٔ نقصان خرد — خردی که در حال پیشروی و گسترش یافتن است.
text.en: The second thread is becoming: before Hegel philosophy claimed to describe a fixed world and movement was no fundamental problem; Hegel’s philosophy is one of becoming, and of the imperfection of reason — a reason in the course of advancing and expanding.
text.nl: The second thread is becoming: before Hegel philosophy claimed to describe a fixed world and movement was no fundamental problem; Hegel’s philosophy is one of becoming, and of the imperfection of reason — a reason in the course of advancing and expanding.

text.fa: خط سوم: فیلسوف از بیرون زندگی به درون آن می‌آید. در فلسفهٔ کلاسیک فیلسوف کسی بود که از بیرون به زندگی می‌نگریست؛ کی‌یرکگور با گفتن این‌که فیلسوف خودش درون زندگی قرار دارد به این نگرش تاخت. «فلسفه‌ورزی نوعی عمل وجود داشتن است.»
text.en: The third thread: the philosopher moves from outside life to inside it. In classical philosophy the philosopher looked at life from outside; Kierkegaard attacked this by saying the philosopher is himself inside life. "To philosophize is a way of existing."
text.nl: The third thread: the philosopher moves from outside life to inside it. In classical philosophy the philosopher looked at life from outside; Kierkegaard attacked this by saying the philosopher is himself inside life. "To philosophize is a way of existing."

text.fa: و حکم کلی او دربارهٔ ارزش فلسفه: «هیچ نظام فلسفی‌ای دیرزمانی نمی‌پاید، ولی به اعتقاد من فلسفه دارای بالاترین ارزش است، یعنی سازمان بخشیدن به جهان در قالب نوعی بینش.» پس نظام‌ها می‌میرند و کار فلسفه باقی می‌ماند.
text.en: And his general verdict on philosophy’s worth: "no philosophical system lasts long, yet in my view philosophy has the highest value — namely organizing the world into a vision." Systems die; philosophy’s work remains.
text.nl: And his general verdict on philosophy’s worth: "no philosophical system lasts long, yet in my view philosophy has the highest value — namely organizing the world into a vision." Systems die; philosophy’s work remains.

text.fa: در پایان درس‌ها به زمان خودش می‌رسد: امروز، از راه تضادی دیالکتیکی، ساختارگرایی در حال مقابله با اگزیستانسیالیسم است. ساختارگرایی را به‌آسانی نمی‌توان تعریف کرد چون در قلمروهای گوناگون ریشه دارد — هم ثمرهٔ اندیشهٔ ریاضی است، هم زبان‌شناسی سوسور، هم انسان‌شناسی لوی-استروس. (متن همین‌جا ناتمام می‌ماند.)
text.en: At the end of the lectures he reaches his own moment: today, through a dialectical opposition, structuralism is confronting existentialism. Structuralism is not easily defined because it is rooted in several domains — the fruit of mathematical thought, of Saussure’s linguistics, of Lévi-Strauss’s anthropology. (The text is left unfinished here.)
